title: Active-nematic rods from noise whose self-made surfactant ring holds a cargo and passes it to both daughters at fission (SIBWD, D diffusion-tested): cargo in/out 12-14 vs 1.4-1.5 with the wall ablated, on 3 seeds, a 1.5x grid and a true dt/2
summary: world.py is c11's active-nematic rods (Cahn-Hilliard droplets with internal nematic order and extensile active stress on a Brinkman-Stokes fluid, after Giomi and DeSimone PRL 2014) with the surfactant s made only on rod pixels (chis=5; 20261026T0200-c34-rodsource) and a cargo c made on rod pixels, long-lived (kcd=0.005) and fast (Dc=1), whose chemical potential ln c + kappa s (kappa=20, positive finite-volume Slotboom flux) makes the rod's own ring exclude it. From uniform noise, rods nucleate (t~50-130), divide by binary fission (13-22 persistent splits, generation 3-4, seeds 0-2, T=1000) and each carries a ring (99-100% of body-frames pass rim/core and rim/out >= 1.5 by signed distance) and holds its cargo (inside/outside median 12.1-14.1, 100% of body-frames >= 2). Both daughters inherit it: 5 frames after a fission 97-100% of daughters hold >= 2x (median 5.5). The kappa=0 ablation, same bodies, lets the cargo spread into the bath (in/out 1.40-1.48, 4% of body-frames >= 2; 0% of daughters). The ring and the wall survive a 1.5x grid (in/out 9.3, ring 100%) and a true dt/2 (15.0 vs 14.6). The zeta=0 twin forms static round droplets with ring and cargo but no division and no motion, so D needs the active stress; B and W do not.

claims.statement: From uniform noise (seeds 0-2), active-nematic rods form, persist as discrete bodies and reproduce by binary fission (22/13/22 persistent splits, generation 3/4/3, merge/split 0.12-0.41); every rod carries a surfactant ring it makes itself (source on rod pixels only; 99-100% of body-frames pass the signed-distance L3 test) and holds a cargo it makes inside that ring (in/out 12-14, all body-frames >= 2), and both daughters of a fission keep the cargo (97-100% of daughters >= 2x five frames after birth).
claims.track: seed 0, track 18 (strip_cargo_seed0_track18.png, strip_ring_seed0_track18.png): born by fission at frame 40, carries its ring and its cargo for 100 frames, divides at frame 140 into tracks 47 and 48, which carry both; the same body with the wall ablated (strip_cargo_kappa0_seed0_track18.png) loses its cargo into the bath

controls_run.B: parent finding 20261026T0200-c34-rodsource: chis=0 ablation gives a diffuse fill (0% of body-frames, rim/core 0.74); here the ring is unchanged on 3 seeds, res15/ and dthalf/
controls_run.W: pack_kappa0/ seeds 0-1 (wall ablation, same bodies): cargo in/out 1.40-1.48, 4% of body-frames >= 2, 0% of daughters; res15/ (1.5x grid, in/out 9.28); dthalf/ (true dt/2, 15.01)
controls_run.D: twin_zeta0/ seeds 0-1: active stress off, round static droplets, 0 splits

claims.bd_control: twin_zeta0/ (zeta=0, the matched passive nematic emulsion, seeds 0-1): no splits and no motion, while ring and cargo remain (rim/core 9-10, cargo in/out 85-122 in the static round droplets); so D is beyond diffusion and B and W are not

limitations: The ring is a quasi-equilibrium coating: the adsorption drift is written against the body field (chis Ds s grad(1-phi^2)), so B rests on RUBRIC L3's self-made-species clause (the source is on rod pixels only). The wall works through an imposed coupling (cargo chemical potential ln c + kappa s), like c31's crawler; neither s nor c acts back on the rods, so the wall does nothing for the rod's own dynamics. Only 21-30% of all cargo sits on rod pixels (10% with kappa=0): the rest has leaked and decays in the bath. Cargo inside a rod is a 1-2 px spine; it survives the 1.5x grid (in/out 9.3) but is weaker there. M is not claimed: no rod moves 3 body lengths between birth and fission (20261026T0300-c34-swimdivide). chis=5, kappa=20, Dc=1 and kcd=0.005 were chosen in short seed-0 sweeps (chis 3/5; kappa 10/20 at Dc 0.2; Dc 1 so that the ablation loses contrast).
